_readme: Body measurements vs model delay knobs. This file is the calibration
input: edit `body_value` from a real camera measurement, then run
`python timing_probe.py --emit` to get the -global fragment that applies
it. Nothing here changes the model's structure - it only fills in the
number that a specific path waits for.
body_value = null means nobody has measured it yet. Do not guess: a
fabricated number is worse than an admitted gap, because it makes a
timing question look answered when it is not.
unit: us or ms. model_event, when set, is an interval this tool can
actually extract from a QEMU trace (see timing_probe.py report mode).
model_event = null means the model has no event for that interval at all.

measurements.note: No model event corresponds to this interval. The capseq delay is a laboratory constant, not this.

measurements.desc: T1 to T2 on the body
measurements.note: Applied 6100000 and measured rise->complete = 6.100 ms, matching the body figure. Doing so exposed two structural bugs that the old 200 us value hid: (1) the falling edge of the request pulse cancelled the latched capture, and (2) capseq_tick refused to complete while the request line was low. With a 6.1 ms exposure both fire on every frame, so the model used to drop the capture and leave a black screen. Both fixed (request-fall-latched).

measurements.desc: peer to handshake on the body
measurements.note: The transport model completes in the same timer tick; there is no interval to calibrate.
Default 2 ms is a laboratory value chosen so a test can observe it. Replace once the body figure is known.

measurements.desc: CVP reset release to boot message

measurements.note: Environment variable, not a QOM property, because the flash shim is not a qdev. Raising it lengthens wall-clock boot under icount (the controller poll loop burns virtual time while the engine waits): at 20 ms the HUD appears near 70 s instead of 55 s. A screenshot taken at a fixed deadline therefore looks black - that is a measurement-window effect, not a boot failure. Verify with a later screenshot before concluding anything.
Environment variable. Datasheet typical is tens of microseconds per word.
Needs a high-speed capture of the actual curtain.
